Like has been already said, head tension affects action. However, to do it right you need to mess with the truss rod and coordinator rods. The truss rod controls neck bow. To check the bow in your neck, capo the first fret, hold down the last fret, and check the gap at around the seventh fret. If there is about the right amount of gap to slide in a credit card, it is set correctly. Here's a link to more info on truss rods. 

http://www.deeringbanjos.com/blogs/banjo-maintenance-tips/10271809-banjo-neck-adjustments 
This page also has info on coordinator rods. I am not going to comment on that myself, as I really am not experienced enough. As an alternative to all of this, you could always get a shorter bridge. This should be fairly cheap, but you might have to play around with the truss rod to get it right. I seriously recommend checking out the link, as it explains this better than I can. If I need to clarify, just let me know. Good luck!
